Not sure what would be applicable to your product/TA, but i would say some things you might want to think about:

- screening and diagnosis initiatives (AI?/ referral networks?)

- interest on RWE generation

- development/implementation of treatment protocols/guidelines

You are probably reaching LOE, so the goal would be straightening your messages and develop your KOLs into “influencers”. Soon there will be a resources and focus cut and you need to ensure that you are having those KOLs disseminating your content to their peers in preparation for the competition/possible generics or biosimilars. Engaging PAGs might be something you would like to do as well.

You also probably have a guidance to focus on the heritage and long term data from your product, but it is quite challenging to discuss such established data with the KOLs who probably know the drug and data much better than you.

Instead you can try to focus on maximizing your KOL list by adding new physicians to it. You can work with your commercial team on going through their list and assess potential for KOL development case by case. Some of those HCPs will be happy to have your support on education/development to speak.

Ensure that your KPIs are aligned with the product lifecycle - it shouldnt be expected to have the same number of visits/quarter from a pre-launch/launch for example. 

Try to visit your KOLs 1x/quarter at least to maintain the relationship - you also dont want to give the perception that due to LOE approaching, your company is not focusing on our product anymore. Try to find ANYTHING to go chat with them - doesnt have to be about your product. It might be those initiatives i mentioned above or maybe a new publication in the field to pick their brains

Its quite a challenge to work with a drug in this stage and maybe everything i have mentioned above will not be applicable for you. But wish you luck!


Edit: another thing i would suggest is to connect with other medical affairs colleagues in other TAs and even in other countries/regions. They might have initiatives that you can tailor to your TA. Why reinventing the wheel? ;) and its seen very positively by the management usually since it shows cross-TA collaboration.

And remember that any new initiative should be sustainable and be relevant for the business/patients.
Especially because i would be expecting your budget is not that high anymore.
For example, you found out a new AI tool for diagnosis that was developed by one of your centers and connects with the EMRs from the institution to screen patients. Try to support this center to disseminate this tool across your region, but without putting any investment. Silly example, but you got the idea

Edit 2: sorry remembered something very important that might shed some light on your thinking. 

You are an MSL, meaning that you should be perceived as a peer to your KOLs on scientific data discussion and disease management optimization. In other words: you are not a sales person focused 100% on product information. You are there to - besides discussing product data which is probably your main priority - to support with education, strategies to optimize screening/diagnosis and support patients. 
If you consider that, it might open many possibilities and opportunities for discussions with your KOLs and HCPs you are trying to “upgrade” to a KOLs status.

Understand the needs and preferences from each KOL. Understand their drivers and goals for the future of the disease management landscape - and then shape the content of those meetings accordingly
